thread:
frank_support: heads-up — customer reported a regression after the canary that started yesterday evening. They say a tiny template tweak causes the invoice-parsing assistant to output garbage. Customer severity: P1 (blocking automated billing).
frank_support: customer repro included, pasting here (redacted):
```
# original template (worked until canary)
Invoice: {{invoice_text}}
Parse: extract line_items, total_amount
```
```
# customer variation (now breaks):
Invoice: {{invoice_text}}
Parse: extract line_items, total_amount.
```
frank_support: note the only diff is a trailing period after `total_amount` in the template. customer says expected output: JSON array of line items. actual output: explanation text + missing numeric totals.
alice_cs: confirmed ticket, customer says they started seeing it right after the deploy at 2026-03-16T19:02Z. They're on Dedicated capacity (reserved) but hitting hosted canary model variant.
ben_eng: which deploy id/commit? can we get the model variant and the exact model/version served to that customer? also any kernel/quantization changes in that rollout?
carlos_runtime: canary id `canary-2026-03-16-19` (deploy-bot shows it). model variant `gptx-mini-q4` switched to new kernel selection heuristics. minor latency bump ~15ms p50, no 5xx spike at first glance. grabbing logs and recent traces.
carlos_runtime: logs snippet (trace id redacted):
```
2026-03-16T19:02:13Z [worker-17] model init: kernel=fast_attn_v2 quant=q4_8
2026-03-16T19:02:14Z [worker-17] serving request trace=tr_abc123 prompt_len=42 output_len=128 tokens=...
2026-03-16T19:02:15Z [worker-17] runtime_warning: kv_cache_mismatch detected for session=svc-445
```
ben_eng: kv_cache_mismatch could cause stale context or shifted tokenization boundaries. did we change tokenization or whitespace normalization?
eve_devex: devex note — we've seen templates break when punctuation is appended after slot names; some older prompt-handling code relied on regex ` total_amount ` which fails if punctuation attached. but we didn't change template processor in this rollout. could be model is now more sensitive to prompt punctuation. quick mitigation: pin template with explicit separator `
---
` or add `
Field: total_amount
` to force a token boundary. e.g. `Parse: extract line_items; total_amount:` (colon) avoids trailing period ambiguity.
frank_support: customer supplied a curl repro. reproduced locally with our hosted API (using staging key) — here's minimal repro (redacted):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
 -d '{"model":"gptx-mini-q4","prompt":"Invoice: $TEXT\nParse: extract line_items, total_amount.","max_tokens":200}'
```
frank_support: returned explanatory text instead of JSON. trace id returned: tr_abc123 (matches runtime warning).
diana_product: two actions: 1) get canary->prod rollout matrix and confirm which customers were routed to canary variant; 2) choose immediate rollback for affected dedicated customers if we can't ship a safe mitigation. what's the customer contract? do they require us to revert?
alice_cs: customer on a paid dedicated plan but still using hosted model variants for experimentation; they asked for urgent rollback or hotfix. they prefer rollback first.
ben_eng: I can try repro in a dockerized worker with two model builds: pre-rollout vs post-rollout. need the exact model binary tag + kernel config. also will run eval suite using their template set to quantify deviation.
carlos_runtime: I can flush KV caches for that tenant and restart worker instances for the canary pool now. that should fix kv_cache_mismatch if it's transient. permission to restart?
diana_product: approve restart as immediate mitigation, but hold full rollback until evaluation results in 15m. if restart doesn't resolve, escalate to rollback.
deploy-bot: deploy event: id=canary-2026-03-16-19 status=partial rolled out to 12% of traffic at 2026-03-16T19:02:00Z
frank_support: performing restart/flush now, will update customer. also adding their template set to a quick regression run.
carlos_runtime: restarted canary workers and flushed caches for tenant svc-445. monitoring traces.
carlos_runtime: after restart metrics: error-rate back to baseline, kv warnings disappeared, p95 latency unchanged. re-run the curl repro — still returns explanatory text (no JSON). en_eng: since cache flush didn't fix, not transient. this points to model behavior change (sensitive to punctuation). try invoking the older model binary (pre-canary) for A/B. can we route this tenant to previous variant?
carlos_runtime: routing change applied — tenant routed to `gptx-mini-q4@sha256:old` (previous). run curl again...
frank_support: re-run against previous variant: returns expected JSON. customer confirms older variant works.
diana_product: product decision: schedule immediate rollback for the canary kernel changes and start a focused investigation into token-boundary sensitivity. also add a canary evaluation harness that runs a corpus of templates (including punctuation edge-cases) before rollout.
eve_devex: follow-up action for devex: add a template-lint rule that flags slot names followed immediately by punctuation (period/comma) and recommend explicit separators. quick patch ready: add `template_lint` check in the CLI.
ben_eng: root cause hypothesis: kernel/attention change altered tokenization or prompting model behavior which made the model less robust to punctuation-attached slot names. next steps: binary diff, tokenizer unit tests, and expand regression suite.
frank_support: I emailed customer with rollback confirmation and ETA 30m, they're relieved. collecting their full template corpus for us. I'll attach to the incident ticket.
diana_product: creating incident page and postmortem stub. assign owners: ben_eng (invest), carlos_runtime (ops), eve_devex (mitigations).
frank_support: thanks team. I'll keep thread updated with customer replies and any billing impacts.
__note: This thread is a synthetic Slack conversation representing a support escalation about prompt-template sensitivity regression tied to a canary rollout. All participant names are Redwood employees or bots.
